python3.covers: Python 3.x. The union table's readings are already this row's, because notes/DESIGN.md 4.2 gives the latest version the reading wherever two collide -- which is why this row narrows completely and python2 below does not.

python2.covers: Python 2.7. This row is narrowable only in part, and the residue below is the reason -- it is the priced case for giving python2 a parse table of its own rather than a manifest over this one.

residue.why: The shared table reads it as a call, which is py3's reading and the one 4.2 awards when two versions collide. A py2 consumer needs the print STATEMENT, and no manifest supplies a reading -- narrowing runs after the parse.
Read as a tuple whose head is a right shift, again py3's reading. print_statement carries prec.dynamic(-1) so the expression wins; the python ledger records this as a deviation.
Does not parse at all. True/False/None are hard keywords in this table because py3 made them so, and a manifest cannot hand back a parse the table refused.
Same cause as True = 5, and it is a real corpus file: the python ledger carries it as an undeclared gap found in pycrypto.
